title: SYSK Selects: The Star Wars Holiday Special of 1978
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the annual holiday listening episode about the Star Wars Holiday Special (CBS, November 1978). The hosts explain how George Lucas, pitched by CBS executives, agreed to a TV special to keep Star Wars audiences engaged before The Empire Strikes Back; how the Wookiee-centered plot (Chewbacca trying to get home to Kazoo for Life Day) was padded into a variety show with musical numbers, guest stars, and long stretches of untranslated Wookiee dialogue; the troubled production (original director David Coomba quitting, Steve Binder finishing, budget overrun); the broadcast and ratings; the infamous cartoon introducing Boba Fett; the ending with Princess Leia's song; and Lucas's disavowal. Also includes a listener mail segment about invented languages and the Voynich manuscript.

segments.title: Opening banter and Life Day introduction
segments.summary: The hosts open with holiday greetings, Star Wars Day talk, and an introduction to Life Day, the Wookiee celebration held every three years, and to the special's reputation as one of the worst things aired on television.

segments.title: Origins: CBS pitch and Lucas's Wookiee idea
segments.summary: After Star Wars became a hit, CBS executives pitched George Lucas on a TV special to keep audiences engaged before The Empire Strikes Back. Lucas proposed a story centered on Wookiees and their home planet Kashyyyk, with a forty-page Wookiee Bible as background, and his only demand was that the special focus on Wookiees.

segments.title: Variety show format and the production team
segments.summary: The special was built as a variety show, reflecting a format that had been popular but was fading by 1978. Writers and producers included Bruce Vilanch, Lenny Rips, and husband-and-wife team the Welchs; David Coomba directed early segments before leaving, and Steve Binder later finished the job. Hiring the writers of Sid and Marty Krofft's Shields and Yarnell was tied to the wordless approach.

segments.title: Cast reluctance and the untranslated Wookiee dialogue
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how Harrison Ford, Mark Hamill and Carrie Fisher had little leverage and appeared reluctantly. The special opens with roughly ten minutes of untranslated Wookiee dialogue, introducing Chewbacca's father Itchy, wife Mala, and son Lumpy.

segments.title: Lucas's reaction to the Wookiee script and the broadcast
segments.summary: Bruce Vilanch recounts Lucas's cold response to the Wookiee-language idea. The special aired on a Friday in November 1978, drawing about thirteen million US viewers for the second hour, running behind The Love Boat and a Pearl Harbor miniseries. It had been planned as an hour but was extended to two because of advertiser demand.

segments.title: Cooking segment, cantina, and adult-themed hair dryer bit
segments.summary: The hosts describe the padding in the special: Harvey Korman in drag as a cooking show host, Art Carney as a trader bringing gifts, Bea Arthur as a cantina owner singing last call, and a hair dryer virtual-reality insert that is softcore pornographic, featuring Diahann Carroll.

segments.title: Hologram sequences, Jefferson Starship, and the Boba Fett cartoon
segments.summary: A hologram of Jefferson Starship performing Light the Sky on Fire fills time while Imperial troops ransack the house. The hosts then describe the animated segment that introduces Boba Fett, regarded as the high point of the special, in which Luke, R2-D2 and C-3PO encounter Boba Fett.

segments.title: Ending: Han Solo, the stormtrooper, and Leia's song
segments.summary: Han Solo and Chewbacca reach the home village; a stormtrooper trips over logs and falls to his death. The celebration of Life Day follows, with Princess Leia delivering a message of peace and then singing, reportedly at Fisher's insistence. The hosts note Lucas's later claims that he had little to do with the special and that he had promised a home video release that never came.

segments.title: Legacy, MST3K riff track, and further reading
segments.summary: The hosts assess the special as campy and enjoyable, note the missing laugh track, mention the Mystery Science Theater 3000 riff track, and recommend the Vanity Fair article and the book How Star Wars Conquered the Universe. They point to HowStuffWorks Star Wars content.

segments.title: Listener mail: invented languages and the Voynich manuscript
segments.summary: Listener Amy from San Diego writes about the Voynich manuscript podcast episode, suggesting that its language may be shaped by familiar structures and that invented languages are limited by what people already know.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts give contact information and sign off.
